_about: What the template picker's details panel shows for each approved template (K, 2026-10-05: original size, player counts, underground on or off, and what makes the template unique). Keyed by the template's name, as in approved-templates.json. Facts come from the template's own file (src/rmg/templates); the description is written from its structure. Outside generator/, so editing it needs no re-pinning. Fields: originalSizeMin and originalSizeMax (tiles, one side), originalLevels (1 or 2; 2 means the original is a two-level template), playersMin and playersMax, humansMax, underground (a sentence), zones (total) and zonesByKind, description (plain text, paragraphs split by a blank line). original (an object): only the original game's own facts for the template, each confirmed by the online check of TEMPLATE-MATCHING-PLAYBOOK.md section 9 step 10, with its sources: players, humans, humanStartZones, computerStartZones, sizeMin and sizeMax (tiles, one side), sizeNames, levels, zones, zonesByKind, checked (date), source (a list of {what, url}), notChecked. The launcher's Original game specs box reads this block and nothing else; what OmniMapGen allows beyond it stays in the flat fields and the description. originalPreferences: the values the "original template preferences" switch sets (levers, templateChoices, ranges, modContent, leversWithNoEffectOnTemplates).

Coldshadow's Fantasy.underground: Two levels in the original; also plays on one level, with the underground zones on the surface
Coldshadow's Fantasy.description:
A template for 2 to 8 players, on maps from Extra Large (144x144) with an underground up to Giant (252x252) with an underground.

It has 21 zones: 8 start zones, 9 treasure zones and 4 junction zones. Each start zone has a castle for its player, one neutral town and a set of mines (two wood, two ore, and one each of gems, crystal, sulfur, mercury and gold). Each start zone joins one treasure zone that has a neutral town; the road between them is guarded at 36,000 for start zones 1 and 5 and at 12,000 for the other six. The treasure zones meet in pairs at the four junction zones, the junctions meet each other in two pairs, and every junction joins the centre zone, a treasure zone with a neutral town, with a guard of 60,000. The junction zones are underground, each has a gold mine and strong monsters, and in the maps OmniMapGen makes they hold neutral dwellings, mostly dragon dwellings (Crystal Cavern, Magic Forest, Sulfurous Lair and Frozen Cliffs). On a one-level map the junctions lie on the surface.

The original has two start zones for human players and six for computer players only. OmniMapGen lets any player be human, and adds start zones when there are more players than the template has.
Coldshadow's Fantasy.brief: Up to eight players on Extra Large to Giant maps with an underground. 21 zones: 8 start zones, 9 treasure zones and 4 junction zones; each start zone joins one treasure zone, the treasure zones meet in pairs at underground junctions, and the junctions join one centre zone.
Coldshadow's Fantasy.templatePreference: Coldshadow's Fantasy starts every player above ground.

original.humans: At most 2: made for 1 human against up to 7 computer players, or 2 humans against up to 6

originalPreferences.about: What 'Restrict all settings to original template preferences' sets for this template: every lever at its template value (the default, which is the template's own 1x), every setting that offers a Template choice locked to it, size, players and humans inside the original's ranges. Mod content stays the player's own choice. A lever listed in leversWithNoEffectOnTemplates is not measured to do anything on a template (LEVER-TABLE.md, after MapGen Dev's k23), so freezing it changes nothing that is known.
originalPreferences.modContent: the player decides; the template names none

Classic.underground: One level or two, as the Underground setting says
Classic.description:
An ordinary random Heroes map, and the place to start if you are new.

What makes it different: it has no fixed layout. The map is drawn fresh from its size and number of players, and every setting on the other pages (how regions join, portals, guards, treasure, water) changes it. The settings follow the size of the map. A Large map starts from what the original Mini Nostalgia makes: big start regions, few treasure regions, wood and ore mines at the starts and almost none elsewhere. A Huge map starts from the original Nostalgia: more regions, a few mines outside the starts, more guards. Sizes in between blend the two. Pick a size and the settings move to its values; Reset puts them back there.
Classic.brief: An ordinary random Heroes map, drawn fresh from its size and number of players. Its settings follow the map size, from the original Mini Nostalgia on Large maps to the original Nostalgia on Huge ones. Start here if you are new.
Classic.templatePreference: Classic has no start rule of its own, so this reads as Random.

originalPreferences.about: What 'Restrict all settings to original template preferences' and the Reset button set for Classic: every lever at its Template value, which for Classic is the lever's own default; the three settings that offer a Template choice (Guards at portals, Split spawns, Water layout) locked to it. Size, players and humans stay anywhere the generator allows. Mod content stays the player's own choice. On Classic the values depend on the map size: the bands entry below contains them, the generator reads it, and the lobby asks the generator for the values of the size picked (generate-cli --listbands 1 --w W --h H --players N --underground 0|1). The levers listed above are the values on maps of 72 tiles a side and smaller.
originalPreferences.modContent: the player decides; the open layout names none

bands.about: Classic's lever defaults by map size (S320, 2026-11-17). Each anchor is the values that bring Classic to what VCMI 1.7.5's own Mini Nostalgia (side 108) and Nostalgia (side 180) make on the engine's maps, with the middle anchor halfway between them; sizes between anchors blend in a straight line by the map's side, sizes above 180 keep the 180 values, sizes below 108 fade from the lever's own default (at side 72) to the 108 values. zones is the stock zone count (eight of them starts); the generator turns it into zoneCells for the map. The engine keeps its eight start zones and its zone count whatever the player count, so a start zone keeps its size when fewer play: startZoneShare is the anchor's for eight players times players over eight (not below the slider's 0.2), and the zones that are not starts are the stock count less the players. A lever in steps is a choice and takes the nearer anchor's value. Only levers the player has not moved follow the band.

feel.about: How Classic draws each map's feel (S340, 2026-11-19). A map draws a feel f from its seed: 0 an old-school scenario, 1 the Nostalgia band (bands above). Each group of levers takes f plus its own offset, and a lever's value is its band value blended toward its old-school value by one minus the group's feel. A lever's old-school value is drawn between the two numbers listed, the values that put the map at the 10th and the 90th percentile of the original scenarios on the property the lever moves (per ground tile, S226). Levers the player moved are never touched. ends: the share of maps drawn at the old-school end, at the Nostalgia end, and how wide an end is; the rest are drawn anywhere between. offset: how far a group may stray from f.

Classic.oneLine: A plain random Heroes map to start with, and DMB's own Mini Nostalgia and Nostalgia: the settings follow the map size, every player in a region of their own, treasure between, monsters in the ways.

Random.underground: One level or two, as the Underground setting says
Random.description: Random picks one of the templates in this list for you: Classic or any template that takes the map's size, players and levels. The pick comes from the map's seed, so the same seed gives the same template. Any setting you leave on "Template" follows the template it picks; Reset puts every setting back on "Template".
Random.brief: Picks one of the templates in this list for you, and the same one every time for the same seed.
Random.templatePreference: Random plays one of the listed templates and takes that template's rule: above ground on Coldshadow's Fantasy, Random on the open-layout entries.

originalPreferences.about: What the Reset button sets for Random: every lever at Template, so each is read from whichever template the seed picks; the values listed are the defaults, which is what Classic uses.
originalPreferences.modContent: the player decides; the open layout names none

Random.oneLine: Runs one of the templates in this list at random.

Jebus Cross.underground: One level in the original; with the underground on, the starts stay on the surface and the middle zone goes below, reached through gates
Jebus Cross.description:
Up to four players each start in a big, poorly guarded and rich zone, set up symmetrically around one extra-rich central zone. To reach the middle they must defeat strong passage guards.

What makes it different: players need to reach the middle as soon as possible, even in the first week.

In construction: the middle zone carries far too much treasure.
Jebus Cross.brief: Up to four players each start in a big, rich zone and must defeat strong passage guards to reach the extra-rich middle zone. The middle holds too much treasure for now.
Jebus Cross.templatePreference: Jebus Cross starts every player above ground; on two levels only the middle zone goes below.

Headquarters.underground: One level or two in the original
Headquarters.description:
A template for 2 to 7 players, on a Large map (108x108), with or without an underground.

It has 9 zones: 7 start zones and 2 treasure zones. Each start zone has a castle for its player, one neutral town and a set of mines (two wood, two ore, and one each of mercury, sulfur, crystal and gems), and each is limited to one town type: Rampart, Tower, Castle (two zones), Dungeon, Necropolis and Conflux. Every start zone has two roads out, each guarded at 45,000: one into a large treasure zone of rough ground with two neutral castles (Stronghold or Fortress), two wood mines, two ore mines and a gold mine, and one into a smaller treasure zone of sand with a mine of each rare resource and a gold mine. Both treasure zones have strong monsters, and they join each other with a guard of 45,000.

In construction: an approximate version, not yet playtested.
Headquarters.brief: Up to seven players on a Large map. 9 zones: 7 start zones, each limited to one town type, and 2 treasure zones that every start zone joins by a guarded road. An approximate version, not yet playtested.
Headquarters.templatePreference: Headquarters starts every player above ground; on two levels both treasure zones go below.

Golems Aplenty.originalSizeNames: Small to Large, one level or two
Golems Aplenty.underground: One level or two in the original
Golems Aplenty.description:
Up to four players.

What makes it different: Golem Factories. In the original scenario the wizards to the south have finally left their valley after a millennium of experimenting with golems. This leaves the local warring lords an opportunity to move in and grab the generators. If you can become the first lord to amass enough golems, you will have a definite advantage. Here the neutral zones hold Golem Factories, with golems among the guards.

In construction: about 50 percent built; the Golem Factories and the golem guards are new and not yet played.
Golems Aplenty.brief: Up to four players. The original scenario says: 'This leaves the local warring lords an opportunity to move in and grab the generators.' This one is full of Golem Factories and golem guards. In construction.
Golems Aplenty.templatePreference: Golems Aplenty starts every player above ground.

lakes.label: Lakes
lakes.oneLine: A few inland lakes; land all the way round the map.
lakes.description:
A land map with a few lakes scattered inland. The map edge is all land, so every player walks wherever they need to go; the lakes are obstacles to go round, with treasure on their shores and sometimes a boat.

Good for a first water map: nothing is cut off, and a hero never needs a ship.
lakes.brief: A few inland lakes; land all the way round the map.

coastal.label: Coastal
coastal.oneLine: A sea along one, two or sometimes three sides of the map; the starts there move inland.
coastal.description:
Land with a sea along one, two or sometimes three sides of the map, by seed. Players whose start would fall in the sea are moved inland. Shipyards and boats let a hero sail along the coast to treasure and to the other players.

Play it as a land map with a back door: most fighting happens on land, and the sea is the long way round.
coastal.brief: A sea along one, two or sometimes three sides of the map; the starts there move inland.

continental.label: Continental
continental.oneLine: Sea all round the edge and one big land mass in the middle.
continental.description:
One large continent surrounded by sea on every side. All players start on it and can walk to each other; the sea round the edge carries the water treasure, sea banks and the occasional island reached by boat.

A land map with a rich shore: worth a ship once the land is settled.
continental.brief: Sea all round the edge and one big land mass in the middle.

mediterranean.label: Mediterranean
mediterranean.oneLine: A sea in the middle with land all the way round it.
mediterranean.description:
A sea in the middle of the map, ringed by land. Players start on the ring and can walk round it to each other, or sail across the middle for a shortcut and the treasure out on the water.

The centre is the prize and the fastest road; the long walk round is the safe one.
mediterranean.brief: A sea in the middle with land all the way round it.

highland.label: Highland
highland.oneLine: A land map cut by wide rivers with a few narrow fords.
highland.description:
A land map split by wide rivers into separate continents. One river runs through a map up to Large, two on Extra Large, three on the biggest maps. Each river is crossed only at a few narrow fords, so armies meet at those crossings.

Hold the fords and you hold your continent: a map of bottlenecks, after the Highland map of Age of Empires.
highland.brief: A land map cut by wide rivers with a few narrow fords. In construction: the fords look slightly too narrow and too uniform.

islands.label: Islands
islands.oneLine: Every player on an island of their own; boats are the only way across.
islands.description:
Every player starts on an island of their own with open sea between them. Each start has a shipyard and a boat on its shore, and sailing is the only way to reach anyone else.

A naval map: scout by sea, and carry your army across when you are ready.
islands.brief: Every player on an island of their own; boats are the only way across.

archipelago.label: Archipelago
archipelago.oneLine: Many islands: one per player and the rest neutral, for whoever sails there first.
archipelago.description:
Many islands. Each player starts on one, and the others are neutral, holding towns, mines and treasure for whoever sails there first.

A race by boat for the free islands before the fighting starts. Needs about a quarter of a small map under water.
archipelago.brief: Many islands: one per player and the rest neutral, for whoever sails there first.
